review.human: Brian, declared human sponsor in the governing Pantheon thread
dissent: Tellus admitted rigor, architecture, network, identity, data, and security as six orthogonal advisory lenses; this does not establish stakeholder standing, approval, or authority.
Tellus also admitted user-experience and humanism; both share the human-outcomes facet, so their complementary agreement is retained as correlated rather than independent evidence.

Tellus admitted network, distributed-systems, Rust engineering, test-harness engineering, and live verification for the compiler cohort; network and distributed-systems share one distributed-communication facet, while Rust and test-harness engineering share one lifecycle-process facet, so their agreement is not counted as independent convergence.
A local subprocess adapter is a bounded first deployment, not a decision that Rune must remain process-coupled rather than expose a future service protocol.

Version one reports process-contract confinement honestly: fixed binaries, cleared environment, bounded channels, no caller-selected paths, and no intentionally passed workspace, credential, or network capability do not by themselves form an operating-system sandbox or prevent access available to Pantheon's process identity.

Chronos owns the maturity path from process-contract confinement through stronger local sandboxing and immutable artifact provenance to supervised local service, authenticated remote service, or WASI-style capability confinement when actual scale, distribution, or threat evidence justifies each transition.
The adapter returns private review material and may never publish it or treat a successful projection as human acceptance.

rosetta.intent: let Pantheon submit one exact reviewed authoring request to the deployment-owned Rune author and return its exact questions, typed refusal, or private Scry-and-Smith-qualified projection packet without shell authority, semantic invention, or publication
outcomes: one bounded exact request is correlated with one deployment-owned Rune author invocation and one exact response
questions-pending and typed author refusals are returned as valid owner outcomes rather than repaired or collapsed into transport failure
a projection packet is returned only when its request, canonical Rune, Scry IR, Smith compatibility, Rust projection, compiler identities, and digests remain internally consistent
timeout, malformed output, excess bytes, identity mismatch, or process failure returns an actionable adapter refusal with no admitted candidate
every outcome names the configured confinement level and never represents process-contract controls as an operating-system sandbox
no path grants workspace mutation, publication, approval, task mutation, rollout, or ambient shell authority
rosetta.who: Pantheon's bounded Rune capability adapter, the deployment configuration owner, the Rune author component, and the accountable human reviewer
rosetta.what: one headless component request from exact private authoring bytes to an exact private Rune-author outcome
rosetta.when: after structured intent and explicit holes exist and before any candidate is published or used as executable authority
rosetta.where: a bounded Pantheon-to-Rune capability boundary using only the configured deployment-owned transport
rosetta.why: agents need the deterministic authoring toolchain without receiving general shell access or bypassing Rune's refusal and human-review boundaries
rosetta.how: validate and digest bounded request bytes, invoke only the pinned Rune author with an empty ambient environment and bounded channels, classify its closed response, verify identities and byte digests, report the deployment's real confinement level, and return one private typed result
rosetta.extent: version-one local authoring transaction under explicitly reported process-contract confinement; no claim of operating-system sandboxing, prose interpretation, ensemble authority, executable selection by the caller, intentionally passed workspace or network capability, Vellum publication, approval, task effect, go-no-go, or rollout
examples: an incomplete J1 UADD request returns fifteen typed questions and no candidate
a reviewed complete request returns canonical Rune, Scry IR, a complete Smith compatibility report, and target-verified Rust in one private packet
a timed-out or malformed Rune author response becomes an adapter refusal and cannot be presented as an author verdict

oversized, non-file, mutable-after-check, or caller-tool-selected input refuses before Rune invocation

rosetta.intent: invoke only the deployment-owned Rune author over bounded private channels

arguments, environment, duration, stdout, and stderr remain closed and bounded

the invocation records process-contract confinement and does not claim that clearing environment or omitting bindings removes ambient filesystem or network access inherited from Pantheon's operating-system principal
process completion alone makes no claim about the Rune author outcome

rosetta.extent: one invocation under process-contract confinement; no retry, shell, caller workspace path selection, operating-system sandbox claim, or publication
examples: Rune author receives the admitted request on stdin and returns one JSON result on stdout
